NameError.explanation: Python reached a word it has never seen before. Every name has to be created before it can be used - by assigning to it, by defining a function, or by importing it.
NameError.cause: Usually a spelling mistake, or using a variable on a line that runs before the line that creates it.
NameError.example:
print(totl)      # Python has never seen 'totl'
total = 10
print(total)     # this works, and it comes after the line that made it

UnboundLocalError.explanation: You read a variable inside a function, but that same function also assigns to it further down. Assigning to a name anywhere in a function makes it local to that function for the whole function, so the earlier read finds nothing.
UnboundLocalError.cause: Trying to change a variable from outside the function without saying so.

TypeError.explanation: You asked Python to do something with a value that does not support it - like adding a number to a piece of text, or calling something that is not a function.
TypeError.cause: Very often a number that is really text: input() always gives you text, even when the person typed digits.
TypeError.example:
age = input("Age? ")
print(age + 1)        # text + number
print(int(age) + 1)   # turn the text into a number first

ValueError.explanation: The kind of value was right but the value itself was not usable. Python understood what you asked for and could not do it with that particular value.
ValueError.cause: Most often int() or float() being given text that is not a number.
ValueError.example:
int("twelve")   # the right kind of thing, the wrong value
int("12")       # this works

SyntaxError.explanation: Python could not understand the shape of your code, so it stopped before running anything. Nothing in the file ran at all.
SyntaxError.cause: A missing colon, an unclosed bracket or quote, or = used where == was meant. Look at the line ABOVE the one Python names - an unclosed bracket is only noticed on the next line.
SyntaxError.example:
if x > 5      # missing colon
    print(x)
if x > 5:
    print(x)

IndentationError.explanation: Python uses indentation to decide which lines belong together. The spaces at the start of this line do not line up with anything.
IndentationError.cause: Mixing different amounts of indentation, or forgetting to indent the body of an if, a for or a def.

TabError.explanation: Some lines are indented with tab characters and others with spaces. They can look identical on screen and mean different things to Python.
TabError.cause: Pasting code from somewhere else into a file that uses the other kind of indentation.
TabError.example:
def f():
    print(1)   # spaces
	print(2)   # a tab - looks the same, is not
# Use spaces everywhere. This editor inserts spaces when you press Tab.

IndexError.explanation: You asked for an item at a position that does not exist. A list of 3 items has positions 0, 1 and 2 - there is no position 3.
IndexError.cause: Counting from 1 instead of 0, or looping one step too far.
IndexError.example:
items = ["a", "b", "c"]
print(items[3])    # there is no fourth item
print(items[-1])   # the last one, whatever the length

KeyError.explanation: You asked a dictionary for a key it does not have. Unlike a list, a dictionary will not invent a value for a key that was never added.
KeyError.cause: A typo in the key, or reading a key before anything put it there.

AttributeError.explanation: You used a dot to ask a value for something it does not have. The value on the left of the dot is not the kind of thing you thought it was.
AttributeError.cause: Often a function that returned None: a method that changes a list in place usually gives back None rather than the list.
AttributeError.example:
names = ["b", "a"]
names = names.sort()   # sort() returns None, so names is now None
names.append("c")      # None has no append
names.sort()           # sort in place, and keep the list

ZeroDivisionError.explanation: Something was divided by zero, which has no answer in mathematics either.
ZeroDivisionError.cause: A count or a length that turned out to be 0 - often an average of an empty list.
ZeroDivisionError.example:
scores = []
print(sum(scores) / len(scores))   # len is 0
if scores:
    print(sum(scores) / len(scores))

ModuleNotFoundError.explanation: Python could not find the module you tried to import. Either the name is wrong, or that module is not available here.
ModuleNotFoundError.cause: A spelling mistake, or an outside library that is not installed in this sandbox.
ModuleNotFoundError.example:
import radnom      # spelled wrong
import random      # this one exists
# random, turtle, math, json and datetime all work here.

ImportError.explanation: The module was found, but the specific thing you asked for is not inside it.
ImportError.cause: Importing a name that the module does not define, usually a spelling mistake.
ImportError.example:
from math import squareroot   # no such name
from math import sqrt         # this is what it is called

FileNotFoundError.explanation: Python looked for that file and it was not there. Your program can only see files that are in your project.
FileNotFoundError.cause: The file has not been added to the project yet, or the name does not match exactly - including capital letters.
FileNotFoundError.example:
open("Data.txt")   # the file in the project is called data.txt
open("data.txt")   # names must match exactly

PermissionError.explanation: Python was not allowed to open that file. Programs here may only read and write files inside their own project.
PermissionError.cause: Trying to reach a path outside the project, such as one starting with / or containing ..
PermissionError.example:
open("/etc/passwd")   # outside the project
open("notes.txt")     # a file in your own project

EOFError.explanation: input() waited for someone to type a line and the input ended instead. There was nothing left to read.
EOFError.cause: Asking for more input than was given, often an input() inside a loop that never stops.

RecursionError.explanation: A function called itself over and over until Python gave up. Every call takes a little memory, so there is a limit.
RecursionError.cause: A recursive function with no base case, or one whose base case is never reached.

AssertionError.explanation: An assert statement checked something and it was false. assert is a way of saying "this must be true at this point", and it was not.
AssertionError.cause: The program reached a state the author did not expect - which is exactly what the assert was there to catch.
AssertionError.example:
total = -5
assert total >= 0, "total should never be negative"
# The message after the comma is shown, so write one.

StopIteration.explanation: next() was called on something that has run out of items. A for loop handles this for you; calling next() by hand does not.
StopIteration.cause: Calling next() more times than there are items.
StopIteration.example:
numbers = iter([1, 2])
next(numbers)
next(numbers)
next(numbers)                  # nothing left
next(numbers, None)            # give a default instead

OverflowError.explanation: The result was too large for the kind of number being used. Whole numbers in Python can be enormous, but decimals cannot.
OverflowError.cause: Repeated multiplication or exponentiation with decimal numbers.
OverflowError.example:
10.0 ** 1000    # too big for a decimal
10 ** 1000      # whole numbers have no such limit

MemoryError.explanation: The program asked for more memory than it is allowed to use.
MemoryError.cause: Building a list that grows without limit, usually in a loop with no stopping condition.
MemoryError.example:
items = []
while True:
    items.append("x")   # grows forever
# Give the loop a condition that eventually becomes false.

UnicodeDecodeError.explanation: A file was read as text, but its bytes are not text in the encoding Python assumed.
UnicodeDecodeError.cause: Opening an image, a sound file or another binary file as if it were text.
UnicodeDecodeError.example:
open("logo.png").read()          # not text
open("logo.png", "rb").read()    # read the raw bytes instead

JSONDecodeError.explanation: The text you handed to the json module is not valid JSON, so it could not be turned into Python values.
JSONDecodeError.cause: A missing comma or bracket, single quotes instead of double, or an empty file.
JSONDecodeError.example:
json.loads("{'a': 1}")    # JSON needs double quotes
json.loads('{"a": 1}')    # valid

KeyboardInterrupt.explanation: The program was stopped from outside while it was running. Nothing is wrong with your code.
KeyboardInterrupt.cause: Pressing Stop, or the run reaching its time limit.
KeyboardInterrupt.example:
# Nothing to fix. If the program was in a loop that never ends,
# give the loop a condition that eventually becomes false.

NotImplementedError.explanation: A function was called that is deliberately left unfinished - its body raises this on purpose.
NotImplementedError.cause: Usually a method a base class expects a subclass to fill in, or a placeholder nobody came back to.

OSError.explanation: Something the operating system was asked to do failed - opening a file, making a folder, or similar.
OSError.cause: A path that is not valid here, or a file operation that is not allowed inside the project.
OSError.example:
open("C:/Windows/notepad.exe")   # not reachable from here
open("my_notes.txt", "w")        # a file in your own project
